newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian parliament to move debates to cafeteria.
newsitem.headline: Canadian parliament to move debates to cafeteria.

text.p: After over 80 years of bluster and heated debates, the building that houses Canada's House of Commons is about to get a facelift while its members take their business to what is now a parliamentary employees cafeteria.

As part of a C$265 million program to spruce up Ottawa's Parliament Hill, the House of Commons will leave its usual abode in the Centre Block of Parliament in 2002 and move to the West Block, a building several hundred meters away, Public Works Minister Diane Marleau said on Monday.

The West Block cafeteria will be demolished and a temporary chamber will be constructed in the courtyard to allow Parliament to continue to function while the Centre Block undergoes extensive renovations.
"We are building an atrium for the House of Commons," public works spokesman Jean Leroux said.
Members of the House of Commons would not receive any free meals while they legislate in the cafeteria, he said.
When asked where parliamentary employees would be fed during the renovations, Leroux responded: "We'll have to find a corner somewhere."
Once the House of Commons is ready to move back into its old quarters, the Senate will take its place in the West Block cafeteria for four years beginning in 2006.
The move to the new chamber will be the first time Canada's Parliament has sat outside of Centre Block since the building was gutted by fire in February 1916.
